scene.label: Act 5, Scene 2
scene.title: SCENE II. Rossillon. The inner court of the Countess's palace.
scene.location: Rossillon. The inner court of the Countess's palace.

lines.text: Good Monsieur Lavache, give my Lord Lafew this letter; I have ere now, sir, been better known to you, when I have held familiarity with fresher clothes; but I am now, sir, muddied in Fortune's mood, and smell somewhat strong of her strong displeasure.
lines.plainText: Good Monsieur Lavache give my Lord Lafew this letter I have ere now sir been better known to you when I have held familiarity with fresher clothes but I am now sir muddied in Fortune's mood and smell somewhat strong of her strong displeasure

lines.text: Truly, Fortune's displeasure is but sluttish, if it smell so strongly as thou speak'st of. I will henceforth eat no fish of Fortune's buttering. Pr'ythee, allow the wind.
lines.plainText: Truly Fortune's displeasure is but sluttish if it smell so strongly as thou speak'st of I will henceforth eat no fish of Fortune's buttering Pr'ythee allow the wind

lines.text: Nay, you need not to stop your nose, sir. I spake but by a metaphor.
lines.plainText: Nay you need not to stop your nose sir I spake but by a metaphor

lines.text: Indeed, sir, if your metaphor stink, I will stop my nose, or against any man's metaphor. Pr'ythee, get thee further.
lines.plainText: Indeed sir if your metaphor stink I will stop my nose or against any man's metaphor Pr'ythee get thee further

lines.text: Pray you, sir, deliver me this paper.
lines.plainText: Pray you sir deliver me this paper

lines.text: Foh, pr'ythee stand away. A paper from Fortune's close-stool to give to a nobleman! Look here he comes himself.
lines.plainText: Foh pr'ythee stand away A paper from Fortune's closestool to give to a nobleman Look here he comes himself

lines.text: My lord, I am a man whom Fortune hath cruelly scratch'd.
lines.plainText: My lord I am a man whom Fortune hath cruelly scratch'd

lines.text: And what would you have me to do? 'Tis too late to pare her nails now. Wherein have you played the knave with Fortune that she should scratch you, who of herself is a good lady, and would not have knaves thrive long under her? There's a quart d'ecu for you. Let the justices make you and Fortune friends; I am for other business.
lines.plainText: And what would you have me to do 'Tis too late to pare her nails now Wherein have you played the knave with Fortune that she should scratch you who of herself is a good lady and would not have knaves thrive long under her There's a quart d'ecu for you Let the justices make you and Fortune friends I am for other business

lines.text: I beseech your honour to hear me one single word.
lines.plainText: I beseech your honour to hear me one single word

lines.text: You beg a single penny more. Come, you shall ha't; save your word.
lines.plainText: You beg a single penny more Come you shall ha't save your word

lines.text: My name, my good lord, is Parolles.
lines.plainText: My name my good lord is Parolles

lines.text: You beg more than word then. Cox my passion! Give me your hand. How does your drum?
lines.plainText: You beg more than word then Cox my passion Give me your hand How does your drum

lines.text: O my good lord, you were the first that found me.
lines.plainText: O my good lord you were the first that found me

lines.text: Was I, in sooth? And I was the first that lost thee.
lines.plainText: Was I in sooth And I was the first that lost thee

lines.text: It lies in you, my lord, to bring me in some grace, for you did bring me out.
lines.plainText: It lies in you my lord to bring me in some grace for you did bring me out

lines.text: Out upon thee, knave! dost thou put upon me at once both the office of God and the devil? One brings thee in grace, and the other brings thee out.
lines.plainText: Out upon thee knave dost thou put upon me at once both the office of God and the devil One brings thee in grace and the other brings thee out
